The *Ajitattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 402) is a verse narrative preserved in the *Therāpadāna* section of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya, recounting the biographical background and meritorious deeds of the elder (thera) Ajita [SuttaCentral]. Modern accessibility of the text is reflected in the SuttaCentral database, which registers five translations in five different languages [SuttaCentral].

No direct canonical parallels are recorded in the SuttaCentral metadata, but computational text-reuse analysis shows significant formulaic and doctrinal continuity within the Pali tradition and across Buddhist literature [DharmaNexus]. Internally, DharmaNexus registers 327 matching passages across 63 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The highest concentration of shared text appears in the commentary to the *Theragāthā* (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, parts 1 and 2), followed by shared stock phrasing in adjacent and thematic poems of the *Therāpadāna*, including the *Sabbadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 401), *Upasivattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 407), *Bākulattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 398), and *Yasattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 553) [DharmaNexus]. Beyond Pali, automated algorithmic alignments identify passages with shared motifs in the Sanskrit *Kaṭhināvadāna* as well as Tibetan translations such as the *Ārya-maitreyaprasthāna-nāma-mahāyāna-sūtra* (D0198) and the *Ārya-pradīpadānīya-nāma-mahāyāna-sūtra* (D0204), although these cross-linguistic matches reflect machine-detected textual commonalities rather than curated parallels [DharmaNexus].
